name: few_indicators_gate
hypothesis: An at-most-one-of-six detector (lower edge of the peak). ReLU unit 773 = relu(-3.54 a1:1 - 4.17 a2:1 - 4.41 a3:1 - 2.27 a4:1 - 3.72 a5:1 - 4.16 a6:1 + 1.52 a4:2 - 0.07 a1:2 + 0.21 a5:3 - 4.47) on z-scored inputs. In indicator terms its pre-activation is about +12 to +16 when no attribute takes its first value, and each first-value indicator subtracts 4.9-8.8. Evidence (train, n=345, full sample): active on 19/19 count-0 and 70/70 count-1 rows, on only 7/113 count-2 rows (pairs a1&a4 and one a1&a6, activation <= 0.52) and on 0/143 rows with count >= 3. Its -7.61 readout drives low-count logits to between -99 and -12. Alone it ranks the classes with AUC 0.67.

name: descending_count_ramp
hypothesis: A linear ramp that falls with the number of first-value indicators (upper edge of the peak). The ten direct input->output edges give each attribute's first value a contribution 7-12 lower than its other values (a1 -10.2, a2 -8.2 vs a2=2 / -11.9 vs a2=3, a3 -12.1, a4 -7.6/-6.9, a5 -10.0, a6 -12.2). Evidence (train, full sample): ramp + output bias lies in [21.3, 25.7] at count 0, [8.6, 18.2] at count 1, [-3.5, 7.9] at count 2 and below -3.7 for every count >= 3 row, so it crosses zero between two and three indicators. Weights are not uniform: a3 and a6 (binary attributes) carry the largest drops, so count-2 rows involving a3 or a6 sit closest to zero. Alone it ranks poorly (AUC 0.62) because counts 0-1 score highest.
reason: no readout edge to output 0; train restore gain < 0.02

name: few_indicators_gate
hypothesis: A fewer-than-two-indicators gate. Write I_k = 1 when attribute k takes its first value (a3:2 = 1-I3 and a6:2 = 1-I6, since a3 and a6 are binary). In these terms node 217 computes ReLU(13.02 - 8.77 I1 - 7.32 I2 - 6.57 I3 - 6.43 I4 - 9.36 I5 - 7.15 I6 - 0.20[a1=3] + 0.39[a2=3]), a near-uniform weighted count of active indicators (weights 6.4 to 9.4) subtracted from 13. It outputs about 13 when no indicator is active, 3.5 to 7.0 when exactly one is, and zero once two or more are. The one leak: the lightest pair (I3+I4) leaves at most +0.41, so the gate fires weakly on 6% of count-2 configurations. Evidence (train, n=345): node 217 ranges 12.82-13.40 at count 0, 3.46-6.98 at count 1, 0-0.41 at count 2, and exactly 0 at count>=3; sensitivities are about 0.8-1.15 for the six indicator columns and about 0.03-0.05 for a1:3 and a2:3, which are negligible.

name: descending_count_ramp
hypothesis: A descending linear count ramp. The direct input-to-output connections sum, in rule-indicator terms, to 20.80 - 8.72 I1 - 9.45 I2 - 5.25 I3 - 10.01 I4 - 9.04 I5 - 11.95 I6 - 0.53[a1=2] - 0.45[a2=3]. a3 and a6 enter through both of their one-hot columns, which combine into single indicator weights. Each active indicator subtracts 5 to 12, and the weights are not uniform: I6 is heaviest (11.95) and I3 lightest (5.25). With the output bias (-1.20) the ramp is +18.6 to +19.6 at count 0, +6.7 to +14.4 at count 1, -3.3 to +5.6 at count 2, and at most -3.41 at every count>=3 (train). It forms the upper edge of the response: three or more active indicators always switch the output off. Evidence: closed form, plus per-count ranges on the train split (n=345).
reason: no readout edge to output 0; train restore gain < 0.02

name: a4_a5_first_value_pool
hypothesis: A4/a5 first-value pool (with an inert a4:2 sub-unit). Write I_k for 'attribute k takes its first value'. In indicator form node 389 = ReLU(-0.744 + 3.793 I4 + 3.317 I5 + 0.492 [a5=4] - 0.0006 u), where u = node 2443 = ReLU(0.997 [a4=2] - 1.281) is identically zero on the whole domain (maximum pre-activation -0.284), so the a4:2 branch is inert (and its readout weight is -0.0006 anyway). With neither a4 nor a5 at its first value the pool outputs 0 (pre-activation -0.744 or -0.252); a4=1 alone gives 3.05 (3.54 when a5=4), a5=1 alone gives 2.57, both give 6.37. The pool is therefore a rectified, near-additive count of the two rule indicators I4 and I5, which the downstream gate does not receive directly. EVIDENCE: Train split (n=345, full sample): node 2443 is 0 on every row; sensitivity of the pool to a4:2 is 0.0, to a4:1 0.86, a5:1 0.71, a5:4 0.10. The pool takes exactly five values on train: 0 (176 rows), 2.573 (a5=1, 62), 3.049 (a4=1, 57), 3.541 (a4=1, a5=4, 25), 6.366 (a4=1 and a5=1, 25).

name: linear_count_ramp
hypothesis: Linear descending count ramp. In indicator form the direct input-to-output connections sum to 16.73 - 8.89 I1 - 8.08 I2 - 8.41 I3 - 1.66 I4 - 6.19 I5 - 8.73 I6 (exact; a6 enters through its complement a6:2 with +8.73, the same signal inverted). Every first-value indicator lowers the score by 6 to 9, except I4 (-1.66), whose shortfall is made up at the root by the pool readout (-0.888 x Pool, i.e. about -2.7 for I4 and -2.3 for I5). The ramp falls approximately linearly with the number of active rule indicators. EVIDENCE: Train split (n=345, full sample): sensitivities equal the absolute weights (a1:1 4.25, a2:1 3.82, a3:1 4.20, a4:1 0.77, a5:1 2.69, a6:2 4.36), as expected for a linear map. Indicator-form least squares fit over all 432 configurations is exact (residual 5.5e-14): 16.73 - 8.89 I1 - 8.08 I2 - 8.41 I3 - 1.66 I4 - 6.19 I5 - 8.73 I6.
reason: no readout edge to output 0; train restore gain < 0.02
